title: QBR - Orion Dataworks - Health Check
summary: Quarterly health check focused on usage trends, cost spikes in June, recent latency incidents during peak ETL windows, and roadmap alignment for caching/batching improvements. Agreed next steps: share detailed cost breakdown, schedule Dedicated capacity review, run targeted benchmark on 4k context with Priya, and send SOC2 and data residency notes.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. This is Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. We got Priya from our SE team as well. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Maya Patel: Hi Jordan, hey Priya, good to see you. Busy month but good.
[00:10] Jordan Lee: Awesome. Quick agenda  usage/cost review, reliability incidents in June, roadmap and feature ask, then action items / next steps. Sound good?
[00:18] Claire Zhang: Yep, go for it.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: Priya, do you want to kick off with the reliability notes?
[00:23] Priya Nair: Sure. So we looked at the incident on June 11th where you had elevated tail latency around 17:30 UTC during your nightly ETL. The root cause was a burst of long-context requests that pushed up queueing on the shared host pool. We saw CPU pinning on a few workers and some KV-cache thrash  sometimes transcribed as k-v cash in our logs, so lol  but basically cache eviction during a high concurrency spike.
[00:46] Luis Ortega: Yeah that was the one. We also saw retries from the orchestrator which amplified the traffic. We were running 2x the normal batch size for one job and it cascaded.
[00:55] Priya Nair: Exactly. Recommendation: enable prefix caching for that job and lower the max batch size for the route during the ETL window. We can also move those jobs to a dedicated pool during the 18:0002:00 window.
[01:08] Maya Patel: Dedicated sounds ideal but cost is the sticking point for us, right  we saw that June bill jump and we need more granularity on where the tokens went.
[01:18] Jordan Lee: Totally. We prepared a cost breakdown  I uploaded a short PDF in the meeting notes (cost_report_Jul.pdf). Quick high-level: 60% of the increase was from long-context generation (>=2k tokens) and 25% from a small set of routes that spike during ETL. The rest was standard growth.
[01:33] Claire Zhang: Can you slice that by project/team? We suspect the analytics team is the big driver.
[01:38] Jordan Lee: Yes. We'll send a per-route per-team view. Action item for me.
[01:41] Priya Nair: One note  you mentioned using quantized models in prod. There are a couple of quantization profiles we can recommend that preserve quality for retrieval-augmented prompts but lower token cost. For example, switching from fp16 to 4-bit Q4 when latency isn't the critical path.
[01:58] Luis Ortega: Is there any quality regression risk? We're doing customer-facing summaries.
[02:02] Priya Nair: Small risk, usually on edge cases. We'll run a quick A/B on a 1k sample. If you want, we can do a shadow test for two weeks.
[02:10] Maya Patel: That would be good.
[02:12] Jordan Lee: Moving on to throughput: your 95th pct latency has improved month-over-month but the variance during the ETL window is still bad. Priya, you wanted to show the benchmark results?
[02:21] Priya Nair: I did a quick internal run  benchmark_results.csv  we ran a 4k context test on Render-XL and saw that with prefix caching enabled and continuous batching tuned to your seq length distribution, p95 drops from ~420ms to ~180ms for tokens generation under similar load. These are synthetic but promising.
[02:40] Claire Zhang: 180ms p95 sounds great. How much does that change cost?
[02:44] Priya Nair: It depends  caching reduces duplicate compute so effective tokens billed per request drop by 10–30% depending on prompt overlap. The throughput improvements let you use smaller dedicated pools for same QPS, so long-term cost savings.
[02:56] Luis Ortega: We're also concerned about data residency and logs. Our legal team flagged retention of request metadata  we need assurance around audit logs and KMS integration.
[03:05] Jordan Lee: Understood. We'll share the SOC2 and KMS notes after the call. Priya, can you attach the private deployment checklist?
[03:12] Priya Nair: Yep, sending link in chat (private_deploy_checklist.pdf). Note: for VPC/private we can sandbox the ETL jobs entirely on a Dedicated pool with customer-managed KMS.
[03:22] Maya Patel: That raises the question  timeline. If we want dedicated for ETL in Q4, what's the procurement lead time?
[03:28] Jordan Lee: Typically 46 weeks from approval for capacity reservation provisioning, plus any networking work. If you need on-prem it's longer.
[03:35] Claire Zhang: Okay we should align this with our Q4 roadmap.
[03:38] Jordan Lee: On the roadmap items: we're shipping a smarter auto-batcher in Q3 and expanded observability in Q4  more per-token attribution and per-route SLO dashboards. That should help you correlate cost to routes without manual slicing.
[03:51] Maya Patel: Nice. About the auto-batcher  will it be compatible with our existing canary setup? We need to avoid surprises.
[03:58] Priya Nair: Yes, it's opt-in and plays nicely with rollouts/canaries. You'll be able to tune thresholds and fallback to previous behavior.
[04:05] Luis Ortega: One more ops detail  during the June spike we saw some 5xx errors from the gateway. Is there a commit or release note we can pin to that time?
[04:14] Jordan Lee: We do have a maintenance window on June 10th where a routing change happened, but the major factor was the workload surge on the 11th. We'll correlate logs and send a brief timeline.
[04:23] Claire Zhang: Great. Can we also get an itemized list of recommended configuration changes for our prod routes?
[04:28] Priya Nair: I'll put together a config playbook: per-route max_batch_size, prefix_cache settings, and suggested model/quantization profiles.
[04:35] Maya Patel: Perfect. For success criteria  what should we measure to call this QBR a win?
[04:40] Jordan Lee: Reduce ETL-window p95 latency by 30% and reduce the token cost per ETL run by 20% within two monthly cycles. Also no more repeated 5xx incidents.
[04:51] Maya Patel: Sounds reasonable.
[04:53] Jordan Lee: Okay, let's walk through next steps and owners.
[04:56] [09:00] Jordan Lee: (note  jumped ahead in the call due to scheduling) I'm back, sorry for the brief rejoin.
[09:05] Claire Zhang: No problem.
[09:08] Jordan Lee: Action items recap  send cost breakdown, config playbook, SOC2/KMS docs, schedule Dedicated capacity review, and run benchmark with your sample.
[09:18] Priya Nair: I'll own the benchmark run and the config playbook. We propose a targeted 4k context benchmark next Tuesday, Aug 4th, at 14:00 UTC. Does that work for you?
[09:29] Maya Patel: Works for me. Luis?
[09:30] Luis Ortega: Fine.
[09:32] Priya Nair: I'll also kick off a two-week shadow test for Q4 quantization changes once we agree on the sample.
[09:40] Maya Patel: Okay. Jordan, can you send the procurement timeline and a quote estimate for a small dedicated pool for the ETL window?
[09:48] Jordan Lee: Yes. I'll include a ballpark and a follow-up with a finance-ready quote.
[09:53] Claire Zhang: Any competitor mentions? We're also evaluating Bedrock for one microservice.
[09:56] Jordan Lee: Noted  we'll include a short comparison matrix.
[09:59] Maya Patel: Last question  are there any immediate knobs we can flip today to reduce cost while we await the longer changes?
[10:05] Priya Nair: Short-term: reduce max tokens on non-critical routes, enable caching on high overlap routes, and turn down sampling temperature if it's used heavily  tiny wins but additive.
[10:16] Luis Ortega: We'll start with those.
[10:19] Jordan Lee: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule invites.
[10:24] Maya Patel: Thanks all.
[10:26] Claire Zhang: Thanks.
[51:30] [end] Jordan Lee: End of recording, thanks everyone.
